summary.text: James Linderholm is the Democratic candidate for Alabama House of Representatives District 20 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent James Lomax (R).
A Huntsville small business owner who trained as a lawyer in England, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that education funding, Medicaid expansion and infrastructure are his priorities.

paragraphs.text: James Linderholm graduated from Reading School in England and earned a graduate degree from Oxford University in 1985.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Linderholm said he was born in Illinois, grew up in England, studied law at Oxford, and practiced in London and Birmingham, Alabama, before moving to Huntsville in 1991.
He said he opened Huntsville Gymnastics in 1993 and has been a small business owner for over three decades.
The Democratic primary for District 20 was canceled, and Linderholm advanced to the general election without appearing on a primary ballot.
He said he would work to restore education funding, expand Medicaid, and improve roads and utilities in a growing Huntsville and North Alabama.
He also said he supports regular open meetings between legislators and voters and the right to use household solar and return excess energy to the grid without a fee.
